findings.title: Direct-exploit target: injection surface in 'INJ' (raw body)
findings.description: Operator-designated exploitation target: the raw-body parameter 'INJ' on https://0a99002f04dea217827d1a4f002800ad.web-security-academy.net/product/stock (body template with {INJ} marker, 'xml-entities' encoding) is worked through the full exploit chain (UNION extraction, tautology reveal, boolean-blind extraction + credential login).
findings.evidence: designated by the operator via --exploit-endpoint --exploit-body; exploit chain attempts logged below
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements; never build SQL from input.
findings.exploit_summary: Tautology payloads did not reveal additional data on this injection point (no measurable hidden-content growth); detection evidence stands.
findings.inferred_sink:
# Reconstructed from behaviour: injecting a quote produces a database
# parser error, proving the input is spliced raw into the SQL statement.
query = "SELECT ... WHERE col = '" + request_input + "'"   # injectable
rows = db.execute(query)   # -> SQL syntax error when input contains a quote

findings.title: Email-auth posture weakness (SPF / DMARC)
findings.description: The domain's SPF and/or DMARC configuration is missing or weak, enabling email spoofing and phishing impersonation of the domain.
findings.evidence:
SPF: (none)
DMARC: (none)
- No SPF record published: the domain can be spoofed for email impersonation.
- No DMARC record published at _dmarc.<domain>: email-auth policy enforcement is missing.
findings.remediation: Publish a restrictive SPF (~all or -all), publish a DMARC record starting at p=none with a rua= aggregate address, then ramp to p=quarantine and p=reject as you gain confidence.
